title: Staged proxy quarantine rollout with state checkpoint & deterministic rollback hooks
creator: Asha Menon
description: Problem: Private VPC runtime upgrades currently rely on coarse rolling restarts. Edge cases (inflight KV windows, write-heavy tenants, and proxy sticky state) can cause transient 5xxs or require full tenant evacuation. We need a deterministic, policy-driven rollout that minimizes user-visible disruption and provides an auditable automatic rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Upgrade can be executed with zero user-facing errors for >=95% of requests in a representative read-heavy and write-heavy synthetic workload. 2) KV prefix-checkers verify state consistency after each stage; mismatches block the next stage. 3) Automated rollback executes within the configured SLA (<=2 minutes after trigger) and restores traffic with session continuity for unaffected tenants. 4) Terraform module flags exist to opt into staged proxy quarantine per-tenant. 5) Playbook documented with runbook steps and links to dashboards.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Preflight - run terraform plan+validate, snapshot KV checksums and create immutable checkpoint. Stage 1: Shadow mirroring - mirror 10% of traffic to upgraded runtime without changing traffic routing; run consistency validators against mirrored responses. Stage 2: Read-only warmup - shift 30% of read traffic to upgrade path with write quiesce on target instance; monitor KV delta meters. Stage 3: Controlled write ramp - enable writes for 5% canary tenants with circuit-breaker and compensatory write log. Stage 4: Progressive widen - increase write traffic in exponential steps (5%->20%->50%->100%) gated by consistency, latency, and error thresholds. Stage 5: Finalize - demote older runtime gracefully, reconcile checkpoints, and remove shadow mirroring. Each stage must pass automated health gates before advancing.
rollback_plan: Trigger conditions: KV checksum drift > threshold, error rate spike > 0.5% absolute, tail-latency degradation > 40% P99, or operator abort. Rollback steps: 1) Immediately disable traffic to upgraded instances via traffic proxy layer (weighted routing to previous runtime). 2) Re-instate write paths to previous runtime, replay buffered write logs if needed using idempotent apply. 3) Run state reconciliation job using snapshots and compensating transactions for confirmed divergences. 4) Mark upgrade as failed in the operator dashboard and create an incident with automated diagnostic bundle (logs, traces, KV diffs). 5) Initiate a hotfix window if root cause requires code change. The rollback must be orchestrated by the upgrade-controller and have a test-mode that simulates steps in staging.
test_plan: - Unit tests for controller state machine transitions. - Integration tests in staging that run full staged rollout against synthetic tenants with both read-heavy and write-heavy workloads. - Chaos experiments that kill upgraded instances mid-stage and validate rollback completes under partial failure. - KV-consistency fuzzing with randomized writes and crash-restarts. - Terraform acceptance tests to ensure module flags and state snapshots are applied idempotently.
monitoring_and_checks: - KV checksum exporter (per-tenant, per-prefix) + alert on divergence. - Traffic proxy metrics: per-runtime weight, request success rate, 99/95/50 latencies. - Synthetic probes that assert end-to-end generation correctness for known prompts. - Automatic snapshot diff artifacts stored in S3 with retention policy. - Dashboard: Upgrade pipeline view with stage status, gating signals, and last successful checkpoint. - Pagering: alert to oncall if any gate trips during rollout.
notes: - Prefer immutable checkpoints over live schema migrations when possible. - Ensure replay logic for write logs is idempotent and respects ordering constraints. - Coordinate with Console team to expose tenant-level opt-in for staged rollout. - Consider a follow-up to add tenant-level rollback window (grace period where tenant can opt-out).
